summary: Coeur d'Alene National Forest lookout: a 40-foot pole L-4 tower built in 1936 and destroyed in 1960; a 2024 visit found only the footings and two benchmarks.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1960. A 2024 visit found only the footings and two benchmarks.

events.note: A camp was located on the site
Jay Murray named on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page
Mr. and Mrs. Clyde Peacock named

evidence.supports: 1930 camp; 1936 40-foot pole L-4 tower; destroyed 1960; 1946 Peacock
evidence.quote: 1930: camp. 1936: 40' pole L-4 tower. Destroyed 1960. Known lookout personnel: 1946: Mr. and Mrs. Clyde Peacock.

evidence.supports: 6 miles NNW of Wallace, Shoshone County
Mr. and Mrs. Clyde Peacock named for 1946
easy drive up; other visitors on the roads

evidence.supports: 2024 visit found footings and two benchmarks
evidence.quote: We were quickly able to find the footings for this lookout tower as well as two benchmarks.

evidence.supports: nothing else remains; view gone as trees grew up
evidence.quote: nothing else appears to remain at this site

evidence.supports: view gone as the surrounding trees grew up
evidence.quote: even the view is gone now that all the surrounding trees have had time to grow well up and around where the tower once sat

notes_for_editor: Record facts checked and not changed (story wording and evidence quotes were tightened 2026-10-10): name, county (Shoshone), kind (tower), gone status and coordinates (FFLA list) agree with the sources read. The Idaho Fire Lookouts category listing gives an address of Dago Peak, which is not used here. Jay Murray (1937) appears only on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page. The 2024 post is the latest description found; no visit report after it. No photographs found.
